audit.why: 50.57% over 3324 games; packet chart gives Akali level 1, Talon 2 through 5, Akali from 6. That matches the kits: Rake at 2 gives him the first real trade tool, and Perfect Execution plus item scaling flips it back.

audit.whatIsWrong: whys[3] described Shadow Assault on the levels 4-5 row.
audit.why: Shadow Assault is the level 6 spike and already has its own row; 4-5 is where Assassin's Path plus Rake gives him free entries and exits.
audit.corrected: 4-5 row now describes the wall-vault pattern; 6 keeps the Shadow Assault framing with its 100-second rank-1 cooldown.

audit.whatIsWrong: Two fabrications: Noxian Diplomacy called an execute 'under 40% HP', and the shroud implied to answer his damage.
audit.why: Riot's text for Noxian Diplomacy is a targeted stab that crits in melee, leaps from outside it, and refunds health and cooldown only if it KILLS. There is no health-threshold execute. The bleed is Blade's End: his spells stack Wound to 3, and his next attack on a 3-stack target bleeds for heavy damage. Separately, Twilight Shroud makes Akali unable to be selected — that stops the targeted Noxian Diplomacy, but Rake and Shadow Assault's blades are untargeted and pass through the smoke unchanged. Nothing in the current text said either thing.
audit.corrected: Shroud denies his Q, not his W or R. His kill pattern is three Wound stacks into an auto, not a threshold execute.

audit.whatIsWrong: No cooldowns anywhere; dosFull[2] invented a 'fifteen-second invitation'.
audit.why: Rake is 9/8.5/8/7.5/7 and Shadow Assault is 100/80/60. Assassin's Path has no cooldown of its own — the terrain it used goes on a long one, so the punish window is per-wall, not per-spell.
audit.corrected: Rake down means nine seconds at rank 1; fight away from fresh walls.

audit.whatIsWrong: Level chart disagreed on six of seven rows — full read Talon/Skill/Skill/Skill/Akali/Skill/Skill against content and packet Akali/Talon/Talon/Talon/Akali/Akali/Akali.
audit.corrected: Flip the six mismatched full-layer sides to the content values.

audit.why: The kit's derived flags mark knockup on Rake; Riot's description says the returning blades deal bonus damage and slow, with no displacement. I asserted only the slow.

edits.after: Talon's Rake poke plus Assassin's Path wall-jumps let him engage or disengage on his own terms, and three Wound stacks from Blade's End turn his next auto into a bleed that finishes any trade you took at half health.

edits.before: Talon is genuinely dangerous in the opening levels — Rake's poke plus Assassin's Path wall-jumps let him harass you from angles you can't easily punish, and Noxian Diplomacy executes any target under 40% HP. From level 3 through 5 he can chunk you down and disengage safely before you close the distance, so play cautiously around any nearby wall and don't overextend past minion cover.
edits.after: Talon is genuinely dangerous in the opening levels — Rake's poke plus Assassin's Path wall-jumps let him harass from angles you can't punish, and Blade's End bleeds you for heavy damage the moment his spells have stacked Wound three times and he lands an auto. From level 3 through 5 he chunks you and vaults out before you close, so hold ground away from walls and don't overextend past minion cover.

edits.before: Level 6 is close to a coin flip — Shadow Assault grants him stealth and a burst-reset almost mirroring your own kit, so whoever lands the first clean combo usually wins the exchange. Respect his stealth-flank timing and try to bait it out with wards or minion cover before committing your own Shroud engage.
edits.after: Level 6 is close to a coin flip — Shadow Assault gives him stealth and a ring of blades that damages on every pass, and because those blades need no target your shroud will not switch them off. It is 100 seconds at rank 1, so bait it with wards or minion cover, survive the converge, and take the fight that follows.

notes: Killed a fabricated mechanic: Noxian Diplomacy was described as an execute 'under 40% HP'. Riot's text has no threshold — it crits in melee, leaps from range, and refunds health/cooldown only on a kill. The real finisher is Blade's End (three Wound stacks then an auto), which appeared nowhere. Second correction: the shroud stops his targeted Q but not Rake or Shadow Assault, both of which are untargeted and pass through the smoke; this is the decisive interaction of the matchup and was entirely absent. Chart disagreed on six of seven rows and is flipped as one atomic group with the three ratings. The kit's derived flags claim knockup on Rake while Riot's text says slow only — I wrote only the slow; worth a data check. breakdown.wave, tradeGood, tradeBad and dosFull[1].d remain Akali-generic templates I could not ground in Talon's kit inside the length band.
